title: Living Stones Church looking at buying former Century Riverside theater in downtown Reno - NewsBreak
text: Living Stones Church in Reno is looking at purchasing the former Century Riverside 12 theater downtown. The former theater, built in 1999, went on the market in 2024 at $7.75 million. The property last sold in 2016 for $6.9 million, according to county records. "As we explore this potential new space, our vision isn’t just for a church building — it’s for an activated riverfront project — a space alongside the church that could include things like coffee, food, art, retail, a preschool, and other elements that serve the city," the church said in a social media post. The building is a few blocks north of the church's Virginia Street location in Midtown. The non-denominational Christian church has nine locations in Nevada. "For the past 15 years, (Living Stones) has served in Midtown with a heart to be 'In the City, for the City,'" the post on Facebook said. "When we moved in, Midtown was a very different place — but by God’s grace and through collaboration with local businesses, artists, and neighbors, we’ve seen it grow into a vibrant, creative, and community-centered part of Reno." The post said the former theater is being looked at to see if it aligns with the church's mission. "Whether we remain rooted in Midtown or take a step toward a permanent downtown home, our commitment to serving and loving this city remains the same," the post said. This article originally appeared on Reno Gazette Journal: Living Stones Church looking at buying former Century Riverside theater in downtown Reno
